sign_convention.positive_angle: swings a downward-hanging part's tip toward +x (forward)
sign_convention.calf: thigh_angle - knee_flexion (knee bends the heel backward)

canonical_rig.T0436_source: @DennieSeth's skeleton reference, zorder_fix_2026-10-08/dennie_canonical_skeleton_ref.png. That file is not present in this worktree or this card's attachments -- every number below is transcribed from the task card's own body/comment (which record it as measured by seeding the image and snapping to the drawn strokes, confirmed by 1px scanline for the two bars), not re-derived from the source pixels by this round. See docs/design/23-canonical-rig.md "Where these numbers came from."

leg_proportions.projection_reasoning: In this lunge the near thigh points away from the viewer (compressed) while the near shin crosses the view plane (full length), so the near-side ratio (1.78) is a projection artifact rather than anatomy; the far-side ratio (1.11) sits inside the anatomical range (1.0-1.1) and is adopted instead. This REVERSES the general near-side-is-truth rule for THIS pose's legs only -- that rule still holds for the arms (upper_limb_reference_comparison below).
leg_proportions.why_not_applied: thigh_R/calf_R (mirrored to thigh_L/calf_L) already drive the leg geometry of every existing animation (walk_cycle, idle_cycle, sitting_idle_cycle); rescaling them to the adopted fractions would shorten every one of those legs by roughly a third, which is exactly the animation re-derivation this card's scope excludes. Recorded here as the target for the follow-on cards that re-derive each animation's own leg geometry.

upper_limb_reference_comparison.note: Upper arm is already close to the reference (within 0.03 of spine, 'already right'); forearm is about +30% over. Neither is corrected this round, for the same reason as leg_proportions.why_not_applied -- every existing animation drives its forearm length from this same rig entry, and rescaling it is the follow-on cards' business.

lateral_offset_axis.description: A per-part, opt-in sideways (local-x) displacement -- rig_compositor.build_placements's lateral_offset_frac parameter, expressed as a fraction of the torso's own width. Distinct from z-order: z decides which part wins a contested pixel, this moves the pixel itself. Every part defaults to 0.0 (no displacement, no behaviour change) unless named in a caller's own dict; no existing pose module (walk_cycle, idle_cycle, sitting_idle_cycle) passes this parameter, so none of them is affected by this axis existing.
lateral_offset_axis.demonstration_values_note: FIX ROUND (@DennieSeth, 2026-10-08T21:08): the prior round assigned a DIFFERENT offset to each of the four parts (-0.50/-0.20/-0.08/-0.03), which tears each limb chain apart at its own joint -- a proximal part sliding one distance while its distal child slides a different one. Replaced with ONE offset per chain: shoulder_L and forearm_L (the far arm) now share -0.35; thigh_L and calf_L (the far leg) now share -0.06. The magnitude is independently swept, not copied: gen_reference_pose_evidence_T0436.py's sweep (recorded in docs/design/23-canonical-rig.md Sec 3c) holds the figure a single connected silhouette (besides one pre-existing, unrelated fragment baked into calf_R's own art -- a motion-streak mark under the boot, present even at lateral_offset_frac={}, confirmed by removing calf_R from the composite) up to -0.46 for the arm chain and -0.25 for the leg chain; beyond those the chain visibly tears into new fragments. -0.35/-0.06 sit well inside both margins while shoulder_L/forearm_L reach 5349/11189 visible px (vs. a 7163/13532 ceiling at -0.46, where pushing further buys no extra visibility, only risk).
